Let
\[
\Theta
=
zH^2+zH+2Hpq+4pq+4zFE-2Fp^2+2q^2E.
\]
Then
\[
\boxed{Z(R)=k[z,\Theta].}
\]

**Solution.** The defining relations are Lie-type relations, so by PBW the ordered monomials in \(E,F,H,p,q,z\) form a basis of \(R\). In particular \(z\) is not a zero-divisor, so we may localize at powers of \(z\).

In \(R[z^{-1}]\), define
\[
e=E-\frac{p^2}{2z},\qquad
f=F+\frac{q^2}{2z},\qquad
h=H+\frac{pq+qp}{2z}.
\]
A direct check from the relations gives
\[
[e,p]=[e,q]=[f,p]=[f,q]=[h,p]=[h,q]=0,
\]
and
\[
[h,e]=2e,\qquad [h,f]=-2f,\qquad [e,f]=h.
\]
Thus, after inverting \(z\), the algebra splits into the tensor product of the localized Heisenberg algebra generated by \(p,q,z^{\pm1}\) and a copy of \(U(\mathfrak{sl}_2)\) generated by \(e,f,h\).

The localized Heisenberg algebra has center \(k[z,z^{-1}]\), since \([p,q]=z\) with \(z\) invertible gives the usual Weyl algebra argument in characteristic \(0\). The center of \(U(\mathfrak{sl}_2)\) is generated by
\[
\Omega=h^2+2h+4fe.
\]
Therefore
\[
Z(R[z^{-1}])=k[z,z^{-1},\Omega].
\]

Now compute
\[
z\Omega
=
zH^2+zH+2Hpq+4pq+4zFE-2Fp^2+2q^2E-\frac{11}{4}z.
\]
Hence
\[
\Theta=z\Omega+\frac{11}{4}z\in R
\]
is central in \(R\). So \(k[z,\Theta]\subseteq Z(R)\).

Conversely, any central element of \(R\) lies in
\[
k[z,z^{-1},\Omega]=k[z,z^{-1},\Theta/z].
\]
So it has the form
\[
\sum_i a_i(z)\left(\frac{\Theta}{z}\right)^i
=
\sum_i b_i(z)\Theta^i
\]
with Laurent polynomial coefficients \(b_i(z)\). If some \(b_i(z)\) had a negative power of \(z\), multiply by the smallest needed power of \(z\) and reduce modulo \(z\). In \(R/(z)\), the image of \(\Theta\) has nonzero top PBW-degree term
\[
2Hpq-2Fp^2+2q^2E,
\]
so its powers are linearly independent over \(k\) by PBW filtration. Thus no cancellation modulo \(z\) can remove the pole. Therefore all \(b_i(z)\in k[z]\), and the element lies in \(k[z,\Theta]\).

Therefore
\[
\boxed{
Z(R)=k\!\left[z,\;zH^2+zH+2Hpq+4pq+4zFE-2Fp^2+2q^2E\right].
}
\]
